lead.t: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) is a haemodynamic and pathophysiological condition defined by an increase in mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 20 mmHg at rest, as measured by right heart catheterisation (RHC).

snip.t: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) is a haemodynamic and pathophysiological condition defined by an increase in mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 20 mmHg at rest, as measured by right heart catheterisation (RHC).
Pulmonary arterial pressure (PAP): A function of pulmonary blood flow, PVR, and left atrial pressure.
Echocardiography (transthoracic): Pulmonary arterial pressure, cardiac function — Elevated PASP → PAH; pericardial effusion or LV dysfunction noted.
Increased pulmonary arterial pressure will increase the split and the loudness of P2.
Pulmonary Hypertension: Elevated pulmonary arterial pressure, classified into five groups based on underlying causes.
